Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:1.hebrew: התירו - לטלטל דבר שעיקר מלאכתו בחול להיתר — לדבר המותר בשבת — התירו לטלטל לצורך גופו, אם הוצרך להשתמש בגוף הכלי, אבל לא משום שהוצרך למקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:1.english: They permitted - to move an object whose primary function during the week is for a permitted [purpose] — [that is,] for something permitted on Shabbat — they permitted moving [it] for the sake of its own use, [i.e.,] if one needed to use the utensil itself, but not because one needed its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:2.english: And then they permitted - these [objects whose function is for a permitted use] for the purpose of their place.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:3.hebrew: וחזרו והתירו אף מי שמלאכתו לאיסור - והוצרך לו בשבת לגופו למלאכת היתר, ומיהו לא הותרו אלו לצורך מקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:3.english: And then they permitted even [an object] whose function is for a prohibited [use] - and he needed it on Shabbat for itself, for a permitted task; however, these were not permitted for the need of their place.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:4.hebrew: כל הכלים - הללו שאמרנו, חוץ מן המסר הגדול, דלא שרי לא לצורך גופו ולא לצורך מקומו. ואביי דמתרץ הכי, הדר ביה לגבי רבה דאמר לעיל "קורנס של נפחים שנינו", דדבר שמלאכתו לאיסור שרי לצורך גופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:10:4.english: All utensils - These [utensils] that we mentioned, except for the large saw, which is permitted [to be moved] neither for the purpose of [utilizing] itself nor for the purpose of [utilizing] its place. And Abaye, who answers thus, retracted [his position] in favor of Rabbah, who said above, "We learned [the Mishnah regarding] a smiths' hammer," [meaning] that an object whose [primary] function is for a prohibited use is permitted [to be moved] for the purpose of [utilizing] itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:1.hebrew: א"ל רבא מכדי - לצורך התירו בפעם ראשונה:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:1.english: Rava said to him: After all - They permitted [it] for a need the first time.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:2.english: What [difference is there] to me [regarding] itself, what [difference is there] to me [regarding] its place - Both of them are a need.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:3.hebrew: מחמה לצל - שאינו צריך לו עכשיו לא לגופו ולא למקומו, אלא חס עליו שמא יתבקע בחמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:3.english: From the sun into the shade - [That is,] he does not need it now, neither for itself nor for its place; rather, he is concerned about it lest it crack in the sun.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:4.hebrew: עד שאמרו - היינו עוד היתר אחרינא, כל הכלים אפי' גדולים. ומיהו לכדאוקימנא, של היתר אפי' מחמה לצל, ושל איסור לצורך גופו או מקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:11:4.english: Until they said - This is yet another permit: all utensils, even large ones [that require two people to carry]. However, [this applies] according to what we established [above]: [an object whose function is] for a permitted [use may be moved] even from the sun into the shade, and [an object whose function is] for a prohibited [use], for the purpose of [utilizing] itself or its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:12:1.hebrew: אין מטלטלין אותה - בשלמא לדידי, אין מטלטלין אותה לצורך מקומה קאמר, אלא לדידך אמאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:12:1.english: One may not move it - Granted, according to me, it is saying [that] one may not move it for the need of its place; but according to you, why [is it prohibited]?

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:13:1.hebrew: משנה זו - דלעיל, "בראשונה היו אומרין ג' כלים ותו לא", משום דהוו מזלזלים בשבתות, דכתיב "בימים ההמה" וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:13:1.english: This mishna - [That which was taught] above: "At first they used to say three vessels, and no more," because they were treating the Sabbaths with disdain, as it is written: "In those days," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:14:1.english: Rods and poles, etc. - They are mishnayot, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:14:2.hebrew: קודם התרת כלים - מנין האחרון, שהותרו כולן לצורך גופן לאביי, ולרבא אף לצורך מקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:14:2.english: Before the permitting of utensils - [i.e.,] the final vote, when all of them were permitted for the sake of their use according to Abaye, and according to Rava even for the sake of their place.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:15:1.hebrew: לא סידור הקנים - שהיו נותנין במערכת לחם הפנים בין חלה לחלה, להפרידן ליכנס הרוח ביניהן, שלא יתעפשו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:15:1.english: Neither arranging the rods - Which they would place in the arrangement of the showbread between one loaf and another, to separate them so that air would enter between them, lest they become moldy.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:15:2.english: Nor removing them - from the old arrangement [of showbread].

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:15:3.hebrew: דוחה את השבת - אלא נכנס בע"ש ונוטל הקנים, ולמחר מסלק המערכה הישנה ומסדר החדשה בלא קנים, ולמוצאי שבת נכנס ונותן הקנים ביניהן. זו נשנית קודם היתר מנין הראשון, דהא מלאכתן להיתר, וקאסר להו לצורך גופן:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:15:3.english: Overrides Shabbat - Rather, [the priest] enters on Shabbat eve and removes the rods, and the next day he clears away the old arrangement and arranges the new [one] without rods, and after Shabbat he enters and places the rods between them. This [Mishnah] was taught before the permit of the first tally, for their [primary] function is for a permitted [purpose], yet it prohibits them [even] for their own use.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:16:1.hebrew: מקלין דקין וחלקין היו - בעזרה, בפסח שחל להיות י"ד בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:16:1.english: Thin and smooth poles were [there] - in the Temple courtyard, on a Passover when the fourteenth [of Nisan] fell on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:1:1.hebrew: אפיקטויזין - להקיא. שותה משקים ומקיא, ולא לרפואה, אלא להריק את מעיו שיוכל לאכול ולשתות [היום] הרבה, כדאמרינן בפרק חבית. ואף על גב דלא גזור בה משום שחיקת סממנין — דהא לאו לרפואה היא — אסור משום דמתקן גברא:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:1:1.english: Afiktoizin - To vomit. One drinks liquids and vomits, not for healing, but rather to empty his intestines so that he will be able to eat and drink a great deal [today], as we say in the chapter [entitled] Chavit. And even though [the Sages] did not decree against it on account of grinding herbs — since it is not for healing — it is prohibited because [by doing so] he is improving [the condition of] a person.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:1:2.english: Here [it is] his usual way - And behold, it is like one who feeds him and gives him to drink.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:1.hebrew: ליטול בה את הקוץ - אלמא תקוני גברא במידי דלאו לרפואה, דליכא משום שחיקת סממנין, שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:1.english: To extract a thorn with it - Thus, mending a person with something that is not for healing, where there is no [concern] of grinding medicinal herbs, is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:2.hebrew: פקיד - הקוץ הזה אינו מחובר בו, אלא מופקד ונתון שם, והוצאה זו אינו תיקון:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:2.english: Deposited - This thorn is not attached to him; rather, it is deposited and placed there, and this removal is not a repair.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:3.hebrew: הכא לא פקיד - ודמי למלאכה, שמסדרן ומכניסן למקום חבור:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:2:3.english: Here it is not deposited - And it resembles labor, for [one] arranges them and inserts them into the place of attachment.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:1.hebrew: קנה של זיתים - לאחר מסיקתן, צובר במעטן, ושמנן מתאסף בתוכן ונוח לצאת. ויש לו קנה להפכן בו ולבדוק אם כמרו כל צרכן, ומגיען לבית הבד:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:1.english: A reed for olives - After harvesting them, [he] heaps [them] in a vat, and their oil gathers inside them and comes out easily. And he has a reed with which to turn them over and to check whether they have softened as much as needed, and [then] he brings them to the olive press.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:2.english: If there is a knot at its top - Like the stopper of a reed pen.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:3.hebrew: מקבל טומאה - דכלי הוא, לפי שעב בראשו קצת:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:3.english: It is susceptible to ritual impurity - For it is a vessel, since it is slightly thick at its top.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:4.hebrew: ואם לאו - לא דמי לכלי, ובגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:3:4.english: And if not - It does not resemble a vessel, and in the Gemara it explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:4:1.hebrew: ואמאי - כי יש בו קשר בראשו, נהי נמי דקשר משוי ליה מנא, מיהו פשוטי כלי עץ הוא, שאפילו חלול הוא, אין חללו עשוי לקבל כלום:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:4:1.english: And why - When it has a knot at its top, even though the knot renders it a utensil, still it is [among] flat wooden vessels, for even though it is hollow, its hollow is not made to hold anything.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:4:2.hebrew: הופכו ורואה - בחלל ראשו, שמשתייר שם על ידי שהוא פקוק בקשר מן השמן הזב מן הזיתים, ובודק בו אם הגיעו לעצור, וזו היא לו קבלה בחלל שלו. ואם לאו, שאין קשר בראשו, אין השמן נראית שם, מפני שאינו פקוק וכולו חלל, הלכך לאו לקבל הוא עשוי והוי פשוטי כלי עץ. ובין כך ובין כך ניטל בשבת, דהא כלי הוא להפוך בו זיתים:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:4:2.english: He turns it over and sees - in the hollow of its tip, where [some] of the oil that oozes from the olives remains because it is plugged by a knot, and he checks with it whether [the olives] have reached [the stage] for pressing, and this is a receptacle for it in its hollow. And if not — [where] there is no knot at its tip — the oil is not seen there, because it is not plugged and is entirely hollow; therefore, it is not made to hold [anything], and it is [considered] a flat wooden vessel. And either way, it may be handled on Shabbat, for it is a utensil for turning olives.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:5:1.english: The large saw - A large saw that is made to cut beams.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:5:2.hebrew: ויתד של מחרישה - הוא כלי גדול העשוי כסכין, שבו עושין חריץ של תלם המענה — קולטר"א בלעז. דהנך קפיד עלייהו ומייחד להם מקום, דלא חזו למלאכה אחרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:5:2.english: And the blade of a plow - [This] is a large utensil made like a knife, with which they make the groove of the furrow — *coltre* in Old French [a coulter]. For one is particular about these [utensils] and designates a [special] place for them, as they are not fit for any other work.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:6:1.hebrew: אוכלא דקצרי - כלי נחושת העשוי כנפה נקבים נקבים, והוא של כובסים, ונותנו על הבגדים ומזלף בו המים עליהן. וי"מ שמגמרין מוגמר מתחתיו, והבגדים מונחין עליו ומתגמרין דרך הנקבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:6:1.english: A launderer's sprinkler - A copper vessel made like a sieve [with] many holes, and it belongs to launderers, and one places it over the garments and sprinkles water upon them with it. And some explain that they burn incense underneath it, and the garments are placed upon it and are perfumed through the holes.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:7:1.english: A shoemaker's knife - A knife of cobblers.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:7:2.english: And a butcher's knife - A knife of the meat market, with which the butchers cut meat.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:7:3.hebrew: חצינא - דולויר"א. כל הני קפדי עלייהו משום דמפגמי, ומקצי להו בידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:7:3.english: An axe [chatzina] - Doloire [in Old French, a type of carpenter's axe]. [People] are particular about all of these because they become nicked, and [therefore] they set them aside with [their own] hands [i.e., deliberately].

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:1.hebrew: ג' כלים - ותו לא. ולקמן אמרינן דבימי נחמיה בן חכליה בבית שני גזרו על טלטול כל הכלים, כדי לגדור גדר להחמיר באיסורי שבת, מפני שהיו מקילין בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:1.english: Three utensils - And no more. And later on we say that in the days of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah, in the Second Temple [era], they decreed against moving all utensils, in order to build a fence to be stringent regarding the prohibitions of Shabbat, because [the people] were treating it leniently.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:2.hebrew: מקצוע - איזמל שמחתכין בו דבלה. "יעשהו במקצועות" מתרגמינן "באיזמליהון" (ישעיהו מ״ד:י״ג):
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:2.english: Miktzoa - A chisel with which one cuts a cake of pressed figs. [The verse] "he fashions it with planes [bammaktzu'ot]" we translate [in the Targum as] "with their chisels [be'izmeleihon]" (Isaiah 44:13).

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:3.english: Zuhama listeron - A large spoon with which one removes the scum of a pot.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:4.hebrew: וסכין קטן - שחותכין בו לחם ובשר ואוכלין, דהני תדירין בתשמיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:4.english: And a small knife - With which one cuts bread, meat, and food, for these [utensils] are frequently used.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:5.hebrew: התירו - עוד כשראו שחזרו להזהר קצת באיסור שבת, וחזרו והתירו כשנזהרו יותר, וחזרו והתירו. ולקמיה מפרש מאי כולהו הנך התירו:
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:5.english: They permitted - [More], when they saw that [people] had returned to being somewhat careful regarding the prohibition of Shabbat; and they again permitted [more] when they were more careful, and they again permitted [more]. And later on, [the Gemara] explains what all these [instances of] "they permitted" are.

Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:6.hebrew: עד שאמרו - עוד חזרו והתירו את הכל, עד שאמרו: הכל ניטלין חוץ מן המסר הגדול כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 123b:8:6.english: Until they said - They again permitted everything, until they said: All [utensils] may be moved except for the large saw, etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:12:1.hebrew: איתיביה אביי מדוכה - בשלמא לדידי מוקמינן לצורך מקומו. וה"מ לשנויי כר' נחמיה כדשני לעיל, ואביי נמי הוה ידע — דהא משני ליה רבה הכי לעיל — אלא פריך לרבא, אולי יאמר תירוץ אחר. ורבא לא בעי לשנויי כר' נחמיה, דלית הלכתא כוותיה; ורבה דמשני ליה כר' נחמיה — משום דמשמע ליה "אין מטלטלין אותם" בשום ענין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:12:1.english: Abaye raised a challenge to him: A mortar - Granted, according to me [Abaye], we establish [the baraita as referring to moving it] for the need of its place. And [Rava] could have answered like Rabbi Nechemiah, as [Rabbah] answered earlier; and Abaye also knew [this] — for Rabbah had answered him this way earlier — rather, he challenged Rava [thinking that] perhaps he would state another answer. And Rava did not want to answer like Rabbi Nechemiah, because the halakhah is not in accordance with him; whereas Rabbah, who answered him like Rabbi Nechemiah, [did so] because [the phrase] "one may not move them" sounded to him [as meaning] in any manner whatsoever.

Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:12:2.hebrew: הכא נמי מחמה לצל - והא דנקט לקצב עליו בשר, אע"ג דלצורך גופו ומקומו נמי שרי — לאשמעינן דאפילו בהא פליגי ב"ש, דלא שרו מחמת שמחת יו"ט:
Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:12:2.english: Here, too, from the sun to the shade - And [as for] why [the Tanna] mentioned "to cut meat on it," even though [moving it] for its own use or for its place is also permitted — [it is] to teach us that even in this [case] Beit Shammai disagree, for they do not permit [it] on account of the joy of the Festival.

Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:15:1.hebrew: לא סידור קנים - אע"ג דאין שבות במקדש, כמה שבותים אשכחן במקדש שגזרו פעמים לצורך, כי הכא בקנים ומקלות, לפי שהיו מחללים את השבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:15:1.english: Neither arranging [the] rods - Even though there is no shevut [rabbinic Sabbath prohibition] in the Temple, we find several shevutim in the Temple that [the Sages] decreed at times out of necessity, such as here with rods and staves, because they would [otherwise] desecrate Shabbat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:7:1.hebrew: וסכינא דאשכבתא - פירש בקונטרס: סכין שהקצבים מקצבין בה בשר; וי"מ סכין ששוחטין בה, שמקפיד שלא תיפגם. ויש ליזהר שלא לטלטלו אפי' לצורך גופו, דהוי כיתד של מחרישה, דאפי' ר"ש מודה, כדאמרינן בסוף מכילתין (דף קנז'.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:7:1.english: And a butcher's knife [sakina de'ashkavta] - Rashi explained [that it is] a knife with which butchers cut meat; and some explain [that it is] a knife with which they slaughter, for one is particular that it not become nicked. And one must be careful not to move it even for the use of the object itself, because it is like the blade of a plow, regarding which even Rabbi Shimon agrees [that it is muktzeh], as we say at the end of our tractate (157a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:8:1.hebrew: מקצוע של דבילה - לא חשיב אלא כלים דלאו בני קיבול, דהא פשיטא דכוסות וקערות וצלוחיות היו מטלטלין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 123b:8:1.english: A knife for [cutting] a cake of dried figs - [The baraita] only lists utensils that are not receptacles, for it is obvious that they would move cups, bowls, and flasks.
